$comment: MB-27.L2 G-STOR v2 (plan-roof-axis v5 section 2, v8 section 4; operator Q-ROOF: storage measured against the 0.60 line, 780 MiB of the 1,300 MiB budget). Exact, read-only, on the built P3 tree. The step's own pure core (materializeBatch) runs over every parcel in a default_transaction_read_only session. Each of the 440,093 lot rows is sized by lane D2's calibrated tuple model (MB-27L2/dryrun/pgsize.mjs tupleLen: exact datum sizes, alignment, short varlena, pglz and TOAST at 2,032 B). That model reproduces pg_column_size(l.*) on 440,093 of 440,093 stored rows. Sizing is done with the stamps as hex text and as bytea (Q-STOR a). The page fill is next-fit in the LIVE HEAP ORDER (dryrun/fill-order.awk over gstor-cal-full/heap-order.txt; MAXALIGN 8, 4 B line pointer, 8,168 B usable). Calibration: the stored rows fill 93,515 pages in that order against 93,519 actual. Option B saves 84.2 B per row on the built 61-wide rows (measured: 1,616.9 hex vs 1,532.7 bytea); a flat 96 B overstates it because of short-varlena headers and alignment. Reconciled with lane D2's 723 MiB: same method, different row contents. D2 sized v8's SQL model of the width-61 arrays (avg 1,544.3 B with bytea, heap 712.4 MiB). This record sizes the arrays the built tree actually writes (avg 1,546.8 B, heap 728.6 MiB); because the rows sit just above the 5-per-page line, the +2.5 B average moves the fill by +16 MiB. Measured on the landing tree (P3 staged over P3-0 d4bc32377 on origin cfbe3aafa: batch parts 3-5, the 1:4 re-key with its five 0.25 threshold units, the Layer 3 forms, the switchboard confidence and MB-18 (l)). Not in this tree, so not in the figure: the lane K rows, the M-475 and Q-RSM door items and the mechanical keying, which land after P3 (operator Q-ORDa); the final G-STOR before the night re-measures on that tip; the assertion in migration-295.logic.test.ts goes red when the versions move. Script and rows: ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/MB-27L2/gate/gstor-v2-exact.mjs and gstor-v2-exact.tsv.
